summary: An institutional broker platform must execute real-time cross-currency trade settlements while verifying bilateral counterparty risk. Orders above $1,000,000 USD require dual-authorization before routing. Before locking in a trade, the clearing engine must confirm sufficient margin balance in the trading account. Settlements should complete within 250ms under normal market conditions, but if market volatility exceeds a Tier-2 circuit-breaker threshold, the order must transition to a queued settlement state instead of completing immediately. On completion, the system emits ISO 20022 compliant pacs.008 confirmation messages to both counterparties.

business_rules.rule: Orders above $1,000,000 USD require dual-authorization before routing.
The clearing engine must validate sufficient margin balance in the trading account before lock-in.
Settlements must complete within 250ms under normal market conditions.
If market volatility exceeds Tier-2 circuit-breaker thresholds, the order automatically transitions to a queued settlement state.
The system emits ISO 20022 compliant confirmation messages (pacs.008) to both parties upon settlement completion.
"Above $1,000,000" is interpreted as strictly greater than $1,000,000; an order of exactly $1,000,000 does not require dual-authorization.
If the trading account does not have sufficient margin balance, the clearing engine rejects or holds the trade before lock-in and no settlement occurs.
An order that does not receive the required dual-authorization is blocked from routing to the clearing engine.
A settlement that exceeds 250ms under normal market conditions is treated as a performance breach and should be flagged/logged rather than silently accepted.

scenarios.description: Execute a standard cross-currency trade below $1,000,000 with sufficient margin under normal market conditions; settlement completes within 250ms and pacs.008 confirmations are sent to both parties.
scenarios.rationale: Primary documented happy path of the requirement.

scenarios.description: Execute a trade above $1,000,000 that receives dual-authorization from two approvers before routing, then settles successfully.
scenarios.rationale: Documented high-value authorization workflow; involves risk and money movement.

scenarios.description: Verify bilateral counterparty risk is checked and confirmed for both counterparties before settlement proceeds.
scenarios.rationale: Explicitly required as part of the settlement process.

scenarios.description: Submit an order above $1,000,000 without obtaining dual-authorization; the order must be blocked from routing to the clearing engine.
scenarios.rationale: Directly tests enforcement of the mandatory dual-authorization control.

scenarios.description: Submit a trade where the trading account has insufficient margin balance; the clearing engine must prevent lock-in and no settlement occurs.
scenarios.rationale: Prevents settlement without adequate collateral, a core risk control.

scenarios.description: One of two required dual-authorization approvers rejects the order; settlement must not proceed and the order remains unrouted.
scenarios.rationale: Tests partial/failed authorization workflow, not just the all-or-nothing missing case.

scenarios.description: Attempt to settle a trade while market volatility already exceeds the Tier-2 circuit-breaker threshold; the system must reject an immediate settlement attempt and instead force the queued state.
scenarios.rationale: Ensures the circuit breaker cannot be bypassed by direct settlement attempts.

scenarios.description: Submit an order for exactly $1,000,000 USD to verify whether the dual-authorization boundary treats this value as requiring authorization or not.
scenarios.rationale: Tests the exact threshold value of the stated $1,000,000 rule.

scenarios.description: Submit an order for $1,000,000.01 USD (just above the threshold) and confirm dual-authorization is required.
scenarios.rationale: Confirms behavior immediately above the stated threshold.

scenarios.description: Submit an order for $999,999.99 USD (just below the threshold) and confirm dual-authorization is not required.
scenarios.rationale: Confirms behavior immediately below the stated threshold.

scenarios.description: Simulate a settlement that completes at exactly 250ms under normal market conditions and verify it is treated as compliant.
scenarios.rationale: Tests the exact edge of the stated performance requirement.

scenarios.description: Simulate a settlement that takes longer than 250ms under normal market conditions and verify the system flags/logs the performance breach.
scenarios.rationale: Tests behavior when the stated performance SLA is violated.

scenarios.description: Simulate market volatility rising to exactly the Tier-2 circuit-breaker threshold and verify the order transitions to queued settlement state.
scenarios.rationale: Tests the exact edge of the circuit-breaker trigger condition.

scenarios.description: Submit a trade order with a malformed or unsupported currency pair and verify the system rejects it before settlement processing.
scenarios.rationale: Field-level validation of trade input required for cross-currency execution.

scenarios.description: Submit an order missing a required field (e.g., trade amount, currency pair, or counterparty identifier) and verify the system rejects the order with a validation error.
scenarios.rationale: Required-ness validation of order submission fields.

scenarios.description: Verify that the pacs.008 confirmation message emitted upon completion contains all ISO 20022 mandatory fields and is schema-valid.
scenarios.rationale: Directly tests the stated ISO 20022 compliance requirement.

scenarios.description: Execute settlements across multiple different currency pairs (e.g., USD/EUR, USD/JPY, GBP/CHF) and confirm consistent settlement behavior and confirmation messaging.
scenarios.rationale: Validates behavior across differing data/currency states as required for cross-currency execution.

scenarios.description: Execute settlements for counterparties with differing risk profiles/ratings and confirm the bilateral risk verification step behaves correctly for each.
scenarios.rationale: Validates behavior across differing counterparty risk data states.

scenarios.description: Execute a high volume of concurrent settlement requests under normal market conditions and verify each still completes within 250ms and receives correct pacs.008 confirmations.
scenarios.rationale: Validates behavior under varying transaction volume.

scenarios.description: Execute settlements where market volatility fluctuates between normal and Tier-2 threshold states across a sequence of orders, verifying each order is routed to the correct settlement path (immediate vs queued).
scenarios.rationale: Validates system behavior across differing market-condition data states.

negative: Direct settlement attempt during active circuit breaker
data: Fluctuating market volatility states across orders

assumptions: The requirement does not define an explicit requirement ID; REQ-108 (from the document heading) is used as the requirement_reference.
"Above $1,000,000" is assumed to mean strictly greater than; an order of exactly $1,000,000 is assumed not to require dual-authorization.
The requirement does not state the consequence of insufficient margin balance; it is assumed the clearing engine rejects or holds the trade and blocks settlement.
The requirement does not state the consequence of missing or partial dual-authorization; it is assumed the order is blocked from routing rather than auto-approved or auto-escalated.
The requirement does not specify the numeric value of the Tier-2 volatility threshold; scenarios treat it as a configurable trigger point to be simulated rather than a fixed number.
The requirement does not state what happens when a settlement exceeds the 250ms target; it is assumed this is logged/flagged as a breach rather than silently accepted or automatically retried.
The requirement does not enumerate required order fields or supported currency pairs; validation scenarios assume standard fields (amount, currency pair, counterparty identifier) are mandatory.
risks: The requirement does not specify exact validation rules for currency pairs or required order fields, so validation scenarios are based on reasonable inference rather than stated rules.
The requirement does not clarify whether the circuit breaker can interrupt a settlement that is already mid-lock-in versus only pre-lock-in orders, creating ambiguity for SC-7 and SC-13.

The requirement does not specify error messages or recovery workflows for negative scenarios (e.g., rejected authorization, insufficient margin), which may require clarification before detailed test cases are written.
No instruction-like or injected content was found in the source requirement text; none was excluded.
